newsitem.title: USA: Intel at full production, sees robust sales.
newsitem.headline: Intel at full production, sees robust sales.

text.p: Intel Corp., the world's largest semiconductor manufacturer, said Wednesday its chip-making factories were operating at full capacity, a sign that the company's sales were robust.

"My factories are full. We are running pedal to the metal right now. That presumably means sales are pretty robust," Gerhard Parker, executive vice president and general manager of Intel's technology and manufacturing group, told investors at a Montgomery Securities conference here.
Parker said Intel was out of production capacity.
To meet demand for its chips, he said, Intel hopes to squeeze out an additional 10 percent of production from existing fabrication plants next year.
Intel, which is based in Santa Clara, Calif., has grown steadily recently due to strong demand for its popular microprocessors, which power roughly 90 percent of the world's personal computers.
Parker said PC demand looked healthy and said Intel generally agreed with research firm Dataquest Inc.'s forecast that the PC market is growing at about 18 percent a year.
He said Intel needed to reduce the manufacturing costs of its Pentium microprocessor, its most popular product, by about 30 percent a year to keep consumer demand for PCs strong.
He added that Intel was currently ahead of that goal.
Intel's stock, bucking a broad downward trend in the markets, gained $2.25 to $131.625 in heavy trading on the Nasdaq market.
